name: Prehistoric Sites and Decorated Caves of the Vézère Valley
description: Along the Vézère River in France's Dordogne, this valley holds 147 Palaeolithic sites and 25 decorated caves, clustered around Les Eyzies, nicknamed the "Capital of Prehistory". Its star is Lascaux, found in 1940, where about 100 animal figures gallop across the walls in rich colours and lifelike detail. The Cro-Magnon rock shelter, which gave early modern Europeans their name, lies here too.
